provenance.section: StreamedMessage.timestamp — the envelope's server send time, documented as RFC 3339
modifications: timestamp changed from an RFC 3339 value to "2023-02-09 20:19:36.100000000 +0000 UTC m=+91717.525857105". That spelling is not invented: it is Go's default time rendering, which this same venue does use for the heartbeats channel's current_time field, so it is the most plausible way an RFC 3339 envelope field could arrive in an undocumented form.
sequence_num changed from 2 to 0, so the fixture can be the first frame of a scenario.
The second trade was dropped, so the assertion is about one entry.
trades[0] is otherwise unchanged, and its own time is still valid RFC 3339 — the point of the fixture is that the ENVELOPE time is the bad one.

expectation: Parses: the wire schema requires only a non-empty string, because rejecting the whole frame would discard real trades over a misspelled publication time. The adapter emits COINBASE_TIMESTAMP_INVALID, still normalizes the trade (whose own RFC 3339 time is what becomes venueTimestamp), preserves the raw value verbatim in venueDetail.venueMessageTime, and refuses to record it as the channel's lastVenueTimestamp — an unvalidated string may not be reported as a venue time.
